title: March warmth gave no clear leaf-out gap slope for matched oak and beech records in four German samples in 1961-2023
abstract: We tested whether March warmth changes the oak-minus-beech leaf unfolding gap at matched German stations. We paired 88,475 station-years at 3,283 stations in 1961-2023. Four models split North and South and two time periods. Station and year means and winter and April temperature were controlled. March slopes ranged from -0.15 to +0.25 days per degree C. All four adjusted intervals included zero. Planned model and coverage checks also gave uncertain March slopes. Fixed-record bounded date errors permitted either sign. The results do not establish equal species responses or a causal climate effect. Missing visit logs, selected records, shared weather and coarse monthly exposure limit inference. Pollution and daily extremes were not tested. Code, exact source hashes, aggregate evidence, a figure and numerical checks are included; source records stay external.

display.caption: March slopes for the paired leaf-out gap. Bars give four-test adjusted intervals. Winter and April warmth are controlled.

citations.reason: Prior single-species thermal-time tests motivate a distinct paired species contrast. Source records overlap.
Adapt fixed-effect and covariance code mechanics. New biological contrast and season; source network and weather overlap.
